name: Tunisia
notes: Depth: seed pass R001 and second pass R002 (2026-11-11). Scope: earlier calls for a wealth tax (economist Elyès Jouini 2014 and 2020, an L'Économiste Maghrébin editorial, Nawaat 2020, Al Bawsala 2022) and the 2026 wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune, article 50 of the 2026 finance bill, enacted as article 88 of the finance law): the Finance Minister, the Assemblée des représentants du peuple (ARP) and the Conseil national des régions et des districts (CNRD) with their finance committee officers, the parliamentary bloc that asked to restore the article, and civil society (Observatoire tunisien de l'économie, Centre Ali Ben Ghedhahem, Al Bawsala, Oxfam). The geography register has the country root, the two chambers, 6 development regions, 24 governorates and 264 delegations (OCHA COD-AB, CC BY-IGO). The tax adopted on 4 December 2025 (72 for, 14 against, 16 abstentions) is 0.5% on net wealth of 3 to 5 million dinars and 1% above, on immovable and movable property of individuals, with the main residence, professional assets, small cars and bank deposits exempt; the earlier 2023 tax on real estate worth 3 million dinars or more is a property tax and is not counted. The plenary vote is published as a count only; no per-member list was found, so no deputy is recorded from the vote itself. Opponents (the ARP finance committee majority, UTICA, economist Ridha Chkoundali) are in exclusions.csv or not recorded. Seats tab: only the CNRD (77 names on its own list, no party shown, one group); the ARP list on arp.tn has names only, with no bloc, constituency or party, so there is no ARP chart. No poll on a wealth tax was found.
